episode.broadcastScript:
This is The Innovation Pulse for Friday, March 20, 2026. Here's what's happening in A.I. and higher education.
-
Today, academic libraries are emerging as campus A.I. literacy hubs, offering neutral spaces for students and faculty to experiment with tools responsibly.
-
In Insights and Trends today, academic libraries are evolving into what researchers call A.I. sandboxes, neutral spaces where students and faculty can experiment with tools responsibly.

According to Inside Higher Ed, Bryn Mawr College library is using a platform called BoodleBox that gives centralized access to multiple A.I. tools while prioritizing privacy. At West Point, librarians developed a custom curriculum-mapping chatbot. Carnegie Mellon and the University of Pennsylvania offer hands-on A.I. literacy workshops.

Lauren Dodd at Bryn Mawr stated that, quote, A.I. literacy is just a new dimension of information literacy, end quote. The skills librarians have been teaching, evaluating sources, understanding bias, thinking critically about information, apply directly to working with A.I. systems.

BoodleBox, one platform being used, serves over 800,000 users across more than 1,300 campuses. Libraries are positioned as neutral spaces not tied to any single department or discipline, serving everyone from first-year students to doctoral researchers with a tradition of teaching information skills.
-
Turning to Practical Tips, the San Diego Community College District is hosting InnovAItion Day today, March 20.

According to SD City Times, the event brings together faculty, staff, and students to explore responsible A.I. use in education. Student-led panels will feature discussions about A.I.'s role in learning. The district is using the event as an opportunity for cross-campus conversation about A.I. policies and practices.
-
In Insights and Trends, a Jobs for the Future survey finds student A.I. use for education increased from 59 percent in 2024 to 70 percent in 2026.

According to Inside Higher Ed, 48 percent of students seek A.I. guidance from social media versus only 23 percent from educational institutions. This indicates students prefer informal learning channels despite institutional efforts to provide A.I. training.
-
In Ethical A.I., the EU A.I. Act enters full effect for universities in August 2026.

According to The Education Magazine, the regulation classifies A.I.-assisted admissions systems and student performance analytics as high-risk. European universities must demonstrate compliance by August 2026 or face penalties. The regulation represents the most comprehensive A.I. governance framework affecting higher education globally.
-
That's today's Innovation Pulse. Full coverage and source links at innovating higher ed dot com.
